tasks.title: Unify ready-work selection and recommendation explanations
tasks.description:
Outcome: One explainable ready-work selector shared by core, clients and UI.

Current implementation: The selector can prefer currentPhaseId before global priorities. Active ownership and pending returns exist but differ across completion/recap paths.

Implementation responsibility:
- Implement the T462 precedence from one persisted snapshot/caller: owned active work, valid ready return, then globally ready feature -> phase -> task.
- Preserve deliberate phase continuity and explicit temporary detours; remove the current-phase priority exception without creating a global task queue or free worker pool.
- Recommendations are advisory: the orchestrator chooses the next task following planner priorities. With the user's agreement a task may start out of priority order; the planner asks for and records a deviation reason and does not block. Unmet dependencies produce a warning; only the execution lock (T490) blocks a start.
- Filter or explain dependencies, parked/abandoned states, in-progress locks of other sessions and held returns; explain zero-priority/tie cases and every exclusion.
- Expose an availability-extension result for later T493 source/target evidence. Do not make the base scheduler depend on advanced target integration.
- Replace independent recap/completion/MCP/Pi/UI selection with this result and verify parity. Recommendations do not reserve work; start still takes the execution lock atomically.

Acceptance and evidence:
- The same snapshot and caller yield the same candidate/reasons across supported surfaces.
- A higher-priority ready feature wins over unowned current-phase preference; an in-progress task is not silently preempted.
- An out-of-order start with user agreement succeeds and records its reason; a start with unmet dependencies warns.
- No dependency becomes eligible merely because its display priority changed.

tasks.title: Preserve and resume nested interrupted work across phase closure
tasks.description:
Outcome: Durable nested interruptions with reliable task/phase continuation and explicit recovery.

Current implementation: Pause snapshots and deviation stacks already exist; losing the return after temporary phase completion or restart is the reported failure, and a parked task stays owned so a later resume is refused (TASK_OWNED_BY_ANOTHER_SESSION).

Implementation responsibility:
- Persist checkpoint, reason, source task/phase, execution/workspace, temporary target and return condition atomically through the shared service.
- Unwind A -> B -> C as C -> B -> A, even after the temporary phase closes. Revalidate context/eligibility at return and keep blocked returns visible.
- A switch or return leaves the task parked (T490 execution lock): it no longer reserves the task against other agents. A takeover warns and is recorded; a return to a task taken over meanwhile reports the takeover instead of failing.
- The same logical agent reclaims its own parked or abandoned tasks from a new conversation; keep other agents unchanged and expose the return chain/reason in focus and UI.
- Preserve exact full variable-width refs in parked reasons and use stable IDs rather than parsing partial display labels.
- Keep block/defer/wait/cancel distinct. Do not replace this mechanism with another parked-work system or automatic cross-phase dispatch.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Closing a temporary phase never deletes the preserved return.
- A blocked return is explained rather than silently skipped or started.
- A parked task can be resumed by its own agent after restart and taken over by another one with a warning; long refs resolve completely.
